            The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal authority for the formulation of national policies and programmes on Tourism and for the
coordination of activities of various Central Government agencies, State Governments/Union Territories and the Private Sector for the
development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Tourism plays a crucial role in coordinating and supplementing the
efforts of the State/Union Territories Governments, catalyzing private investment, strengthening promotional and marketing efforts and in
providing trained manpower resources.  The main activities of the Ministry include:-

4.         The approach in the 10th Plan aims to stimulate investment and encourage the State Governments to develop unique tourism products. 
The State Governments would use Tourism as a means for achieving their socio-economic objectives and catalyze the private sector to enhance
investment in tourism.  It seeks to enhance the employment potential within the tourism sector as well as to foster economic integration through
developing linkages with other sectors.  The 10
th
 Plan acknowledges the traditionally recognised advantages of developing tourism for the

promotion of national integration, international understanding and the earning of foreign exchange besides recognising vast employment
generating potential of Tourism and furthering the socio-economic objectives of the Plan. It also seeks to provide legislative and regulatory
support for sustainable tourism and protect the interests of both the industry as well as the consumer. It further seeks to involve the rural sector
in the promotion of all rich areas of tourism viz., rural, heritage, adventure and eco-tourism.  It focuses on the development of competitive high
quality products and destinations besides addressing the concerns of growth through resolution of contradictions in policy so as to achieve
inter-sectoral convergence of activities that helps to foster the growth of tourism.

RURAL TOURISM
25.       Tourism growth potential can be harnessed as a strategy for rural development. The development of a strong platform around the
concept of Rural Tourism is definitely useful for a country like 
India
, where almost 74% of the population resides in its 7 million villages. 
Across the world, the trends of industrialisation and development have had an urban centric approach. Alongside, the stresses of urban
lifestyles have led to a "counter-
urbanization "
 syndrome. This has led to growing interest in the rural areas. At the same time, this trend of
urbanisation has led to falling income levels, lesser job opportunities in the rural areas leading to an urbanisation syndrome in the rural areas.
Rural Tourism is one of the few activities, which can provide a solution to these problems. Besides, there are other factors, which are shifting
the trend towards rural tourism like increasing levels of awareness, growing interest in heritage and culture and improved accessibility, and
environmental consciousness. In the developed countries, this has resulted in a new style of tourism of visiting village settings to experience
and live a relaxed and healthy lifestyle. This concept has taken the shape of a formal kind of Rural Tourism.  Ministry of Tourism gives
financial assistance to the State Governments for the Rural Tourism Projects.

through the Government of India
